question: Should OpenClaw core own a per-agent backup/restore/clone flow now, and what credential/session portability policy should it enforce?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but implementing it safely requires product and security intent for secrets, transcripts, destructive restore, archive compatibility, and coordination with broader backup/restore work.

options.title: Sponsor core design first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a design/PR that reuses the existing backup manifest and SQLite snapshot model while defining safe `--agent` and `--as` behavior before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader backup work
options.body: Make the broader backup/restore tracker or encrypted snapshot PR own per-agent semantics, and leave this issue as a requirement until that path explicitly covers clone behavior.

options.title: Defer core clone support
options.body: Decline first-party per-agent clone for now and document the current `agents add` plus manual migration path, accepting that it does not provide full state/session restore.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a design/PR that reuses the existing backup manifest and SQLite snapshot model while defining safe `--agent` and `--as` behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is product/security direction across backup, config, and agent auth boundaries, and steipete has recent adjacent history plus likely routing context.
